abstract: Positivity cannot obstruct the Hodge conjecture on projective varieties, since $\alpha+Nh^p$ is strictly positive for $N\gg0$. It can separate projective from Kähler geometry, where the Kähler analogue fails. We ask whether a rational Hodge class in the interior of a positive cone must be analytic, or must force projectivity. On complex tori the answer depends on the cone. Main Theorem: if a rational Hodge class of degree $2p$, $1\le p\le n-1$, on an $n$-dimensional complex torus lies in the interior of the strongly positive cone, the torus is an abelian variety; the first non-elementary case is $(n,p)=(4,2)$. The proof combines compactness of the centraliser of the complex structure in the Hodge group, Deligne's Cartan-involution criterion, a Wirtinger calibration inequality, and a growth argument showing that interior weak positivity forces $H^1$ to be semisimple. Sharpness: a simple non-projective 4-torus built from a quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$ has rational Hodge classes in the interior of Demailly's positive cone, and they are not analytic. This torus is a compact-type Weil torus for every imaginary quadratic subfield of its endomorphism algebra, but no single Weil structure explains the positivity: on compact-type Weil 4-tori with generic Hodge group, no nonzero degree-4 Hodge class is even weakly positive. On hyperkähler manifolds no $SU(2)$-invariant class is strongly positive in the interior. For the sharpness example, the non-divisorial part of $\mathrm{ch}_2$ of a stable bundle is a nonnegative binary quartic that vanishes only for projectively flat bundles. So one bundle that is not projectively flat would make every Hodge class a Chern class while none is analytic. Bearing on the conjecture: strongly positive Kähler counterexamples on tori are impossible, and positivity-based approaches must use projectivity essentially.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: Revision addressing the v1 review. (1) New Convention 3.1 fixes the hermitian normalisation $H_\alpha$ and the interior criterion $\alpha-\varepsilon\omega^p/p!\in C$; Theorems A and D now quote it, and the Theorem C dual certificate is spelled out (type, weak positivity, orthogonality, non-vanishing, separation). (2) Theorem D: new Lemma 8.0 (antilinear Jordan basis with full proof); step (2) now has the explicit sign $\varepsilon_p=(-1)^{p(p-1)/2}$ and the estimate $b(\mu,\mu)\ge\varepsilon|\mu|^2$ with the metric making the basis unitary; step (4) uses the induced derivation $D_A$ and an explicit constant. (3) Theorem B quotes Milne's Prop. 1.20 (C-polarisations) and his definition of a Cartan involution, and verifies that $G^{(\theta)}(\mathbb{R})$ is compact. (4) Proposition 10.1: added rationality of $\mathrm{NS}$, $\mathrm{Hdg}^4$ and of the summand $K_5$ (via the $\mathbb{Q}$-rational Casimir of $SL_1(B^{op})$), and the lattice/order $\mathcal{O}$ used for isogenies. (5) Section 12 split into 12.A (proved: Props 12.1, 12.2), Corollary 12.3 explicitly marked conditional on a seed bundle, 12.B (open questions and heuristics, no claims) and 12.C (cubic/quintic analogues, Remark 12.4). (6) Abstract shortened to under 300 words. New content: Section 10 paragraph showing that the sharpness torus is a compact-type Weil torus (definite hermitian form) for every imaginary quadratic $E\subset B$, with Weil classes $v_{\ell^4}$ spanning $K_5$; new Proposition 10.2 (with proof) that on a compact-type Weil 4-torus no nonzero class in $\mathbb{R}\omega^2\oplus W_E$ is weakly positive, so the Cor-type symmetry is essential. Section 12.B adds a sketched class-level no-go for rank-2 extension and Serre-subtorus seeds on the CM fibre (heuristics section, not a claim). Supplement adds t29.py, t30.py, t33-t36b.py.
title: Strongly positive Hodge classes force projectivity of complex tori, and weakly positive ones do not
